newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom sees lower rural S.Africa profit.
newsitem.headline: Telekom sees lower rural S.Africa profit.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Tuesday its joint venture with Telkom of South Africa could focus on developing telephone lines in less profitable rural areas.
"It is a possibility, yes," Telekom Malaysia's chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said when asked if the new joint venture would have to extend lines to rural areas.

"On an average 'per line' basis, it (expansion into rural areas) may not be as profitable (as expansion into urban areas), but it will be profitable," Mohamed Said told reporters. He was speaking after Telekom Malaysia signed an agreement with Malaysia media and property conglomerate MRCB for multimedia services.

Telekom Malaysia said on March 28 it would invest around $504 million in a U.S.-Malaysian consortium that is buying a 30 percent stake in the newly privatised South African telecommunications utility Telkom.
Telekom Malaysia's own stake in the deal -- sub-Saharan Africa's largest privatisation project -- amounts to 12 percent.
